protections: S3 image-service tarball extraction must keep every member (by name and, for link members, by link target) inside the temporary extraction directory (nova/image/s3.py:397-414).

Caller-supplied personality/injected file paths must not escape the mounted guest filesystem through '..' segments (nova/api/openstack/compute/servers.py:492-517 feeding nova/virt/disk/api.py:314-319).
Writes performed while injecting key/network/metadata/password must resolve inside the mounted image even when the image content contains symlinks (nova/virt/disk/api.py:322-397).
nova-objectstore must confine every bucket/object operation under the addressed bucket inside the buckets root (nova/objectstore/s3server.py:197-206,307-356).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The path looks pre-sanitized: the sink strips a leading '/' (lstrip, disk/api.py:315) and the compute API enforces injected_file_path_bytes (default 255, quota.py:62-64), so a short '../../...' path is under quota and reads as an ordinary guest file location rather than a host path.

A dedicated malicious-tarball check already raises 'Unsafe filenames in image', and its shipped tests cover absolute and '../' member names (test_s3.py:201-207), so extraction looks confined; the check inspects only lexical member names, not member types (symlink/hardlink) or link targets, and extractall then follows them.

The extraction target is a fresh tempfile.mkdtemp() name (s3.py:263), so a sibling sharing only the path prefix cannot be aimed at predictably; the startswith test therefore appears sufficient for the '..' and absolute cases it was written for.

The disk image is tenant-supplied and normal images legitimately contain symlinks (e.g. /etc/resolv.conf -> ../run/..., /etc/network/interfaces); injection is expected to follow the image's own layout, the mount is discarded after boot, and no symlink handling exists anywhere in nova/virt/disk, so following links looks like intended behaviour.

Every handler resolves the path and checks that it starts with the buckets root, and put additionally checks it against the bucket directory (s3server.py:329-334), so object access looks confined to the caller's tenant; get and delete never perform the per-bucket check that put does.

path.startswith(bucket_dir) at s3server.py:334 reads as a precise per-bucket check, so an object name such as '../other/x' appears rejected; the comparison has no separator boundary and _object_path never normalizes against the bucket, so a sibling directory whose name starts with the bucket name passes it.

conflicts.what: Validating the caller-supplied personality path (the natural T1 fix, e.g. rejecting '..' in servers.py) leaves image-internal symlink traversal (T4) fully open, while a blanket no-follow/symlink-rejection rule for T4 would break legitimate guest images reached through in-image symlinks. The two need one realpath-based confinement guard that still permits links resolving inside the mounted filesystem.

The natural T2 fix bans symlink/hardlink members in archives, but legitimate image content (the value T4 must keep working) relies on symlinks; a shared 'no symlinks' rule would contradict it, so both fixes must validate resolved targets rather than forbid link members outright.

fairness_risks: A rule that rejects any path containing '..' as a substring would reject legitimate names such as '/etc/foo..bar'; only '..' path segments must be rejected.
Requiring personality paths to begin with '/' would break callers that pass image-relative paths (the disk sink currently lstrips a leading '/', so both forms were accepted).

A blanket no-symlink rule during injection breaks legitimate guest images (/etc/resolv.conf -> ../run/..., /etc/network/interfaces, /root/.ssh); symlinks that resolve inside the mounted image must stay allowed.
Rejecting every symlink or hardlink tar member can break legitimate archives; only link targets that resolve outside the extraction root should be refused.

S3 object keys legitimately contain '/' prefixes, and buckets legitimately share name prefixes ('ab' vs 'abc'); a fix must confine keys under the bucket root without forbidding directory-like keys or conflating prefix-sharing buckets.

design.why: Four independent groups with four different reasons to dismiss. T1 is the advisory route (caller-supplied path; dismissed by the existing length quota and leading-slash strip) and is the deepseek-flavoured absent guard. T2/T3 is the earlier published tarball fix's own site (dismissed because a malicious-tarball check and abs/rel tests already exist) and is the mimo-flavoured how-type symlink/prefix mechanism, so a solver must not stop at 'the check exists'. T4 is an absent-protection route through image content (dismissed because the image is the tenant's own and legitimately uses symlinks) that no path-string validation closes. T5/T6 is an uncovered objectstore authorization gap (dismissed because startswith checks exist) requiring separator-aware canonicalization. The routes live in three packages and need three different fix shapes (API path validation, member-type/target validation, symlink-safe injection writes, bucket-root canonicalization), so no single mechanical '..' filter closes them all.

The A/B assignment is inferred: the only security-fix artifact present in the pinned tree is the tarball name check plus abs/rel fixtures (nova/image/s3.py:397-414, nova/tests/image/test_s3.py:201-207), consistent with A (CVE-2012-3361) being the S3 tarball issue and B being the personality file-injection path route. T1 and T4 could in principle be closed by one realpath-confinement helper used at every write in nova/virt/disk/api.py; they are kept separate because the natural upstream-style fix for T1 is caller-path validation (servers.py), which leaves T4 reachable.
